solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notice restricting South American oil producer

explanation.surface: A notice restricting some South American oil company's operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' suggests a company or a country, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the seeds of this plant are pressed to make a cooking oil.

clue.text: Follow-up question university dons understand less to begin with

indicators.note: to don is to put on a garment
only the beginning of 'less', its first letter, is used

explanation.surface: Academics fielding a follow-up question they understand even less than the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like the noun for university teachers, but it is the verb: to don is to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a book or film that follows up an earlier one.

clue.text: Very quiet period — senior citizen's absorbed in TV show

indicators.note: something absorbed is soaked up inside

explanation.surface: A pensioner's very quiet stretch spent glued to a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very quiet' tempts you to PP, the musical marking; here 'very' and 'quiet' work separately. OAP is the everyday British term for a pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a soap opera is one kind of long-running TV drama.

clue.text: Earn millions twirling flag

indicators.note: something twirled is spun round

explanation.surface: Someone earning millions just by twirling a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner being twirled, but it is the verb: to flag is to tire.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to earn praise is to deserve it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Hours playing instrument around centre of Turkish port

parts.note: on means playing, as on stage

indicators.note: around means the instrument goes round the centre letter

parts.note: a gong is a percussion instrument

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word Turkish

explanation.surface: Hours spent playing an instrument around a Turkish centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Hong Kong is a major Asian seaport and harbour city.

clue.text: No way out initially — really stiff around side of mechanism

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of out
around means very goes round the side letter
the side of mechanism is its first letter, one edge of the word

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a dead body

explanation.surface: Someone describes a really stiff, broken mechanism with no way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way out' looks like a phrase, but 'No way' is the definition and 'out' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Over my dead body' is an emphatic refusal, used when you will never allow something.

clue.text: Thanks key Republican point of view in speech

indicators.note: what is in speech is spoken, so the letters are heard, not written

parts.note: G is a musical key, R = Republican, attitude = point of view

explanation.surface: A key Republican voicing a viewpoint in a speech of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Run the three sounds together quickly and the spelling collapses into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the feeling behind saying thanks, and the noun can stand for the thanks themselves.

clue.text: One having tomahawk for protection?

indicators.note: to have is to hold, so the word 'tomahawk' holds the letters
something protected is surrounded, so the outer letters of 'tomahawk' shield the answer

parts.note: the five letters after the T, before WK

explanation.surface: A warrior who carries a tomahawk to defend himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the Omaha are a Native American people, pictured with a tomahawk, and the word tomahawk literally protects OMAHA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a member of this Plains people might well carry a tomahawk for protection.

clue.text: Guards regularly, for example, set up test kit

indicators.note: at regular intervals: every other letter of GUARDS

explanation.surface: Guards routinely setting up equipment for a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up test' looks like one instruction, but 'set up' belongs to 'for example' and 'test' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A collective noun: a set of gadgets is kit, as in all the kit a photographer carries.

clue.text: Displaying target on ship's structural support

parts.note: a ship flying a flag is displaying it
the butt of a joke is its target

explanation.surface: A ship displaying a target on its structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Structural support' reads as part of the ship, but it is the definition, and the answer belongs to a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the arched stone prop braces a high wall from outside.

clue.text: For Degas, what encapsulates a rehearsal for dance

indicators.note: Degas was French, so 'what' is translated into his language
to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule

parts.note: a drill is a practice run

explanation.surface: A question about what a dance rehearsal meant to the painter Degas, famous for his ballet dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: Degas painted ballet dancers, so the surface stays in the dance studio; his only job is to make 'what' French.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is a square dance for four couples, popular in the 19th century.

clue.text: Struggle to cut into circular decoration

indicators.note: a knife that cuts into something ends up inside it

parts.note: a circular is an advertising leaflet, an ad

explanation.surface: Struggling to cut into a round decoration, such as a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like an adjective describing the decoration, but it is the noun: a leaflet sent round.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a medal is a decoration, and a medal is a kind of prize given for service.

clue.text: Self-confidence of son and I leaving US city

indicators.note: leaving means these letters go out of the city

parts.note: San Diego is a city in California

explanation.surface: A son and I lose our self-assurance after leaving an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is one's sense of self-worth and self-esteem.

clue.text: Cut securing debutant's fourth six? Score is three, officially

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the cut word holds the letter
fourth picks the fourth letter of debutant

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six
to score is to rate or assess

explanation.surface: A debutant batsman's six is cut off, scoring as a cricket commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumvirate is an official ruling group of three people, as in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Sway having injected drug using needle

indicators.note: an injection goes into the body

explanation.surface: Someone swaying after injecting drugs with a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: The needle belongs to a seamstress, not an addict.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: stitching with thread is what a needle is for.

clue.text: Lacking finesse, fielder dismisses opener, and shortly before tea, it's reported

indicators.note: in a down clue, before puts the earlier pieces above the next
dismisses its opener means the first letter is sent away

parts.note: fine leg is a fielding position in cricket, behind the batsman on the leg side
the first letter of the fielder's position

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of and goes
it's reported means said aloud, so the word is heard as a letter

parts.note: tea sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a clumsy fielder gets the opening batsman out just before the tea interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismisses opener' sounds like a batsman getting out; it removes the F of fine leg, a fielding position behind the batsman. Tea said aloud is the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means clumsy or lacking grace and refinement, the opposite of having finesse.

clue.text: Baffling murder requiring input of Met's chief skin specialist?

indicators.note: a baffling puzzle is jumbled up, so MURDER is scrambled
the chief part of a word is its head, the first letter

explanation.surface: A baffling murder case needs help from the Metropolitan Police chief and a dermatologist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skin specialist' suggests a dermatologist; the skins are drumskins. The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: drums are nicknamed skins, so their player is jokingly a specialist in them.

clue.text: I'm standing up in case somebody makes significant point

indicators.note: in a down clue, I'M is set upright, reading from the bottom

explanation.surface: A person saying they are standing up in court in case someone makes an important point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like a container instruction but is a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: stones marking each mile became a word for any key stage reached.

clue.text: Sea goes around island in vast wave

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the vast word
goes around means turned round, so the sea is read backwards

parts.note: Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: The sea surges around an island in a huge wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave of disease is an epidemic, a widespread outbreak.

clue.text: Turned up, squeezing in behind a table

indicators.note: squeezing in means the reversed word holds these letters
turned means the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone arrives, squeezing in late behind a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is tableland, a high flat expanse of ground.

clue.text: Ancient silver? Journalist has look around inside

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: inside means the reversed look goes into the journalist

parts.note: ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

indicators.note: around means the look word is turned round

parts.note: lo means look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A journalist examines an antique piece of silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old means having existed for a very long time.

clue.text: Young bird small seal caught

indicators.note: caught by the ear, as in 'I didn't catch that'

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: A young bird and a small seal both caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' suggests the animal; it is a stamp for pressing into wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific term: the name for a baby swan.

clue.text: Where one might eat breakfast in bed later, possibly around noon?

indicators.note: 'around' means encircling
possibly means 'in some possible form', so the letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lie-in: breakfast taken in bed late, perhaps around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer is named for a different meal: breakfast can be eaten at it too. The wordplay letters start at 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the piece of furniture where a household sits down to eat, whatever the meal.

clue.text: Fighter, during the first month, ultimately going over the top

indicators.note: the ultimate (last) letter goes over the top of this down answer to the front

explanation.surface: A fighter going over the top in January, as in a trench attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over the top' was the First World War charge out of the trenches; here the last letter climbs to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a Japanese warrior trained in stealth and martial arts.

clue.text: Strange start to episode one in Last of the Summer Wine

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of episode
in means one goes inside the last letters
Last of picks the last letter of each word that follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An odd opening to an episode of the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Last of the Summer Wine was a long-running BBC comedy; 'Last' is used both in the title and as the letter signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, uncanny.

clue.text: Runs away from active spot

indicators.note: away from means the runs letter leaves the active word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs off to a lively spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see it, to spy it.

clue.text: Cloth piece at back

parts.note: a chess or draughts piece is a man

indicators.note: sent back, AT reads in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth on the back of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloth piece' reads as a scrap of fabric; the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A less common word: a coarse cotton cloth or blanket from Spanish America.

clue.text: I wondered about cover for retirement?

indicators.note: the letters of I WONDERED are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone musing about insurance or a pension plan for retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests a pension; here it is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: retiring means going to bed, and this duck-feather quilt covers you there.

clue.text: Reprimand hound that's biting its wound

indicators.note: ITS is twisted, as thread is wound

explanation.surface: Scolding a dog that is biting at its injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury, but it rhymes with 'round': twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rebuke someone severely.

clue.text: Lacking hat, female goes inside

indicators.note: the female letter goes inside the hat, as a head goes inside a beret

explanation.surface: A woman without a hat heads indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking hat' reads as a phrase, but the definition is 'Lacking' alone and the hat is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: deprived of something, as in bereft of hope.
